sections.h2: What is the fastest path to a closing in Homestead?
sections.html:
Choose how you will sell, get title and lien paperwork in order, and sign a deed that is witnessed, taxed and recorded in Miami-Dade County. The buyer and the state of your title set the pace, since no one gets to skip recording.

Sellers in South Dade tend to weigh three routes. Listing publicly reaches the most people yet depends on a lender's appraisal. A cash purchase drops the lender and often the repair negotiation, a good fit for a house needing work. Selling to family is permitted, but a transfer for money still owes deed tax, and estate-planning transfers have no separate exemption.

  • Check who is on title, including any owner who has died or moved away.
  • Request a payoff letter from each lender.
  • Get the current tax bill and look for unpaid earlier years.

Homestead is a young, family-heavy market where renting is common. The city had 80,737 residents in 2020 and an estimated 86,242 by mid-2025, up from 60,512 in 2010. Owners occupy 48.3 percent of homes, so rentals edge ahead. Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $380,000, and the median rent is $1,674. Average household size is 3.21 people, and 68.8 percent of residents speak a language besides English at home, so bilingual listings and documents help buyers.

Hurricane Andrew hit the city directly in 1992. Keep your permit history and any insurance claim paperwork ready for the buyer and the title company. The city also has designated historic districts and a historic downtown, so ask the city before altering an older building.

sections.h2: Selling a house that has been rented
sections.html:
Many sellers in Homestead are landlords or heirs who never lived in the house, which shapes both the tax story and what buyers ask.

Miami-Dade's property appraiser warns owners not to put a homestead exemption at risk by renting the property. If an exemption was claimed while the home was rented, back taxes can reach ten years, with 15 percent annual interest and a 50 percent penalty. Raise that with a Florida attorney before you sell.

When a tenant lives there, give the buyer the lease early. Under Chapter 83, a tenancy by the month needs 30 days of notice, and an unpaid-rent demand runs three days, leaving out weekends and court holidays.

sections.h2: Deed tax and who must sign
sections.html:
Homestead is in Miami-Dade, the one county with its own deed rate: 60 cents per $100, plus a 45 cent per $100 surtax that does not apply to a document transferring only a single-family dwelling. Everywhere else the rate is 70 cents.

That carve-out makes property type matter. A single-family house generally escapes the surtax, while a duplex does not fit that description. Your closing agent should confirm which applies.

Anyone who signs the deed shares liability for the tax however the contract splits it, and it is paid to the clerk at filing. Under section 28.24 the clerk's first-page recording fee is $5.00. A conveyance of land must be written and signed before two subscribing witnesses, and the statute allows audio-video witnessing.

The exemption you hold stops at closing, and every new owner files on their own. March 1 is the Miami-Dade filing date. Late filings are accepted through the cutoff printed on the TRIM notice, usually 25 days after mailing, and a $15 fee may apply if a Value Adjustment Board petition is needed.

Amendment 3 passed on November 3, 2026. For owners who established Florida residency by December 31, 2026, the top non-school exemption grows to $150,000 for tax year 2027 and $250,000 for 2028. Later arrivals follow different rules, and the school-board exemption stays $25,000. The appraiser can explain how this affects your buyer.

The next January 1 after closing brings a fresh just-value assessment, so the buyer's first bill can exceed yours. Afterward the cap limits yearly growth to 3 percent or CPI change, whichever is smaller.

• Foreclosure: the clerk's sale follows a final judgment by 20 to 35 days unless the plaintiff consents to longer.
  • Probate: a small estate (non-exempt value up to $150,000) or a death more than two years back can use summary administration.
  • Tax certificates: two years after the April 1 of the year a certificate was issued, the holder can ask for a tax deed, so clear old balances first.

Deaths after 2004 trigger no Florida estate tax.

sections.h2: A checklist for landlords and heirs
sections.html:
If you inherited the house or have rented it out, start with title. Confirm who is on the deed, and if an owner has died, find out who has authority to sign. Next, collect every lease, rent record and tenant contact, since a buyer will ask for them. Then call the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser to find out whether a homestead exemption was ever claimed while the house was rented, because that is where back taxes can arise.

With those answers in hand, compare offers on net proceeds. A buyer who takes the house with tenants in place may need less time than one who wants it empty, and a cash buyer who accepts the house as it sits can save you the cost of repairs and the wait for a lender.

After you accept an offer, the closing agent orders title work and asks each lender for a payoff letter. The agent checks the tax bill for earlier unpaid years, prepares the deed and arranges the two witnesses. The Miami-Dade tax collector can give you the amount owed, and the agent pays any open balance from your proceeds.

Recording happens at the clerk's office, where the stamp tax is also paid. How fast that goes depends on the clerk's queue and whether your closing agent files electronically. A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal, but title cleanup and recording still take time, so ask for a written timeline before you commit to a closing day.

faqs.q: Is the deed tax different in Homestead?
faqs.a: Yes. Miami-Dade County has its own schedule. The rate is 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cent surtax that does not apply when only a single-family dwelling transfers.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Homestead house with a tenant inside?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer takes it subject to the lease, so share a copy. Tenancies without a fixed term end on statutory notice, such as 30 days for month-to-month.

faqs.q: Does the buyer get my exemption?
faqs.a: No. The buyer must file by March 1, and assessed value resets after the ownership change.

faqs.q: How are unpaid property taxes handled?
faqs.a: The closing agent pays them from your proceeds. The Miami-Dade tax collector can give you the amount owed, and bills left unpaid go delinquent on April 1.

faqs.q: How long does the deed take to record?
faqs.a: Recording happens at the clerk's office, where the stamp tax is also paid. Speed depends on the clerk's queue and whether your closing agent files electronically.
